text: Study Planner — Change & Enhancement
Specification
Phase 6 Browser Verification  Consolidated Change Log
Document Status
Initial change captured
Change ID
CHANGE-001
Primary Area
Calendar UI / Calendar Data / Interaction Model
Change Type
UI/UX Enhancement + Data Model Enhancement + New Calendar Behavior
Reference Basis
User-provided browser screenshots and verbal requirements
Current Project Context
Phase 6 complete; browser verification is being performed before the next implementation phase.
1. Requirement Summary
The current Study Planner calendar is functionally present but visually too simple compared with the user’s preferred
reference calendar. The desired result is not a purely visual redesign: the Study Planner should adopt the reference
calendar’s richer visual hierarchy, navigation model, calendar metadata, and small date-specific note/event
interactions while preserving the existing application’s real planning, progress, and tracker functionality.
Core principle: the reference HTML/calendar should become the visual and interaction benchmark, while the
existing Study Planner remains the source of real study data and existing application behavior.
2. Current Problem
The current Study Planner calendar shown in the screenshots is comparatively minimal. It provides Monthly/Weekly
switching, date navigation, date selection, and plan awareness, but it does not provide the same visual richness,
information density, contextual navigation, or date-level metadata that exists in the desirable reference UI.
Observed/desired differences include:
 The calendar UI should visually resemble the desirable reference HTML rather than the current minimal calendar
presentation.
 Monthly and Weekly modes should have their own appropriate navigation/header presentation instead of sharing a
generic/simple header treatment.
 Weekly view should clearly communicate the currently selected study week and year.
 Monthly view should clearly communicate the currently selected calendar month and year.
 The calendar should expose meaningful study-cycle information directly on dates, such as Week 1 and Graded
Assignment.
 Small date-specific actions such as Add a note and New Event should exist in the calendar UI and remain visually
lightweight.
3. Desired Calendar UI Direction
The desirable reference UI should be treated as the primary visual reference for the calendar experience. The
implementation should reproduce its overall visual hierarchy, spacing, navigation structure, toggle behavior,
selected-date treatment, and contextual information while adapting it to the Study Planner’s real data model.
3.1 Mode-specific navigation
Weekly mode: The area above the Weekly/Monthly toggle should communicate the current study week, for example
“Oct Week 1 - 2026”. The left/right navigation controls should move between study weeks, not merely arbitrary
calendar weeks, because the Study Planner follows a defined study cycle.
Monthly mode: The area above the Weekly/Monthly toggle should communicate the selected calendar month and
year, for example “October 2026”. The navigation controls should move between calendar months.
The Weekly/Monthly toggle itself should retain the reference UI’s clear, prominent presentation and should make the
active mode immediately obvious.
4. Full-Year Calendar JSON Data
Introduce a dedicated JSON representation for the complete calendar year. The calendar should not depend only on
the generated study-plan files to understand dates. A year-level calendar data source should explicitly represent the
calendar structure for the full year, including months and their dates/days, and provide a place for Study
Planner-specific metadata.
The year-level JSON should be capable of representing:
 The target year (e.g., 2026).
 All 12 months.
 Dates within each month.
 Day-of-week information needed by the calendar.
 Whether a date belongs to the Study Planner’s active study cycle.
 Study week association for a date.
 Study-day number within that study week.
 Special day markers such as the graded-assignment day.
 Date-specific note metadata.
 Date-specific event metadata.
5. Study-Cycle Metadata Example
The Study Planner begins its active study cycle on 2 October 2026. Therefore the calendar data should understand
the study cycle independently from the ordinary calendar month structure.
For the first study week, the intended mapping is:
Date
Study Week
Study Day
Special Meaning
Week 1
Day 1
Study-week start
Week 1
Day 2
Week 1
Day 3
Week 1
Day 4
Week 1
Day 5
Week 1
Day 6
Practice / study-cycle day
Week 1
Day 7
Graded Assignment
The same pattern should continue through the full study cycle: each study week has seven study days, and the
seventh day is identified as the graded-assignment day where applicable. The exact generated-plan rules remain
authoritative; this calendar metadata should expose the study-cycle meaning rather than inventing a second planning
algorithm.
6. Date-Level Visual Hints
When a user interacts with a date, the calendar should be able to show concise contextual labels beneath or around
the date without making the calendar visually cluttered.
 Clicking/activating 2 October should make its study context visible, such as “Week 1” and/or “Day 1”, according to the
final UI design.
 8 October should visibly communicate that it is the graded-assignment day, using a concise label such as “Graded” or
“Graded Assignment”.
 The transition between study weeks should be visually understandable: the end of one week is marked by its graded
day and the following study week begins immediately after it.
 The date metadata should be derived from the calendar/study-cycle JSON rather than hardcoded into the UI.
7. Add a Note / New Event
The desirable reference UI contains two lightweight controls: Add a note and New Event. These should be
incorporated into the Study Planner calendar while keeping them visually compact and contextual.
Add a note: When the user adds a note for a selected date, the note should appear as date-specific calendar content
in an appropriate location around the calendar/date area, similar in spirit to the reference UI. It should remain
associated with the selected date.
New Event: The user should be able to create an event associated with a specific date. The event should then be
represented for that date in the calendar UI.
The exact persistence/storage mechanism for user-created notes and events should be defined during
implementation so that it does not conflict with the project’s existing completion authority or generated-plan
architecture.
8. Functional Preservation Requirements
This change is a calendar enhancement, not a replacement of the Study Planner’s underlying architecture. Existing
functionality must continue to work.
 Existing Monthly/Weekly switching must continue to work.
 Existing date selection and Daily Tracker navigation must continue to work.
 Real plan data must remain the source of study tasks.
 Existing completion persistence through storage.js must remain unchanged.
 Existing progress calculations through progress-engine.js must remain unchanged.
 Existing Reports and Progress navigation must remain functional.
 The study-cycle timing and Fri→Thu behavior must not be silently replaced with a conventional Monday→Sunday
academic week.
 The calendar must not create a duplicate progress engine, completion store, or planning algorithm.
9. Acceptance Criteria
 The Study Planner calendar visually follows the supplied desirable reference closely enough that the current minimal
calendar no longer feels like a separate design.
 Monthly mode has month/year navigation and a clear Monthly/Weekly mode toggle.
 Weekly mode has study-week/year navigation and a clear Monthly/Weekly mode toggle.
 The current study week can be identified from the calendar’s study-cycle data.
 The full target year has a dedicated JSON calendar representation.
 The calendar can identify study week, study day, and graded-assignment metadata for relevant dates.
 2 October 2026 is recognized as Study Week 1 / Day 1.
 8 October 2026 is recognized as the final day of Study Week 1 and its graded-assignment day.
 Notes and events can be associated with specific dates and displayed contextually.
 Existing planner, tracker, progress, reports, and storage behavior continues to work.
 The implementation is validated in a real browser at the required responsive sizes.
10. Implementation Boundary
This requirement should be treated as a combined UI/UX + calendar data model + calendar interaction change. It
may require new files/components for calendar metadata and date-specific notes/events, but the implementation
must first inspect the existing repository and recover/reuse existing calendar architecture before creating parallel
systems.
The final implementation phase(s) for this change should be designed later, after all browser-verification changes
have been collected. Do not prematurely assign this requirement to Phase 7/8 or invent the final phase breakdown
yet.
11. Reference Screenshots
Figure 1 — Current Study Planner calendar UI (Monthly view).
Figure 2 — Reference / desirable calendar UI (Weekly view).
Figure 3 — Current Study Planner calendar UI (Weekly view).
Figure 4 — Reference / desirable calendar UI (Monthly view).
12. Change Log
CHANGE-001 — Calendar UI should be upgraded to match the supplied desirable reference UI while preserving
Study Planner functionality, with a full-year calendar JSON model, study-week/day/graded metadata, mode-specific
navigation, and lightweight date-specific notes/events.
Next update: Future changes must be appended below this change. Existing changes must not be removed unless the user explicitly
requests a requirement revision.
Study Planner — Change & Enhancement
Specification
CHANGE-002  Breadcrumb & Navigation Hierarchy
Change ID
CHANGE-002
Category
UI/UX  Navigation  Information Architecture
Affected Area
Progress and Reports sections
Priority
High
Status
Captured during browser verification
1. Requirement Summary
The Progress section is currently behaving correctly from a navigation and breadcrumb perspective. The problem is
specifically in the adjacent Reports section: its breadcrumb hierarchy does not provide the same clear route back to the
Calendar. The Reports hierarchy should be brought into alignment with the navigation pattern already working correctly
in Progress.
Key requirement: preserve the existing Progress breadcrumb behavior and apply the same hierarchical navigation
principle to Reports. This is not a request to redesign the Progress section; it is a request to correct the Reports section
so both areas follow a consistent application hierarchy.
2. What Is Already Correct
 The Progress section's breadcrumb provides a visible path back to Calendar.
 Progress drill-down navigation works correctly.
 The Mathematics I progress detail page demonstrates a strong navigation pattern: a clear back action plus a
hierarchical breadcrumb that retains the parent path.
 The user explicitly does not want the working Progress behavior disturbed.
3. Current Reports Problem
The Reports landing/detail views currently lack the Calendar level in their breadcrumb/navigation hierarchy. As a
result, Reports does not communicate the same parent-child relationship that Progress communicates.
The expected hierarchy is conceptually:
Calendar → Reports
For deeper report pages, the hierarchy should continue to preserve the parent context instead of dropping the
Calendar level. For example, a deeper report should retain the equivalent of Calendar → Reports → [current report]
where appropriate.
4. Desired Behavior
 Add a Calendar navigation level to the Reports section's breadcrumb hierarchy.
 Make the Calendar breadcrumb/action clickable so the user can directly return to the Calendar.
 Keep the existing Reports label as the current section in the hierarchy.
 For report detail pages, preserve the parent hierarchy while identifying the current report/page.
 Use the same visual language and interaction behavior already established by the working Progress breadcrumbs.
 Do not remove or weaken the existing Progress breadcrumb behavior.
5. Consistency With Progress Drill-Down
The user specifically wants the Reports section to follow the same successful pattern visible in the Progress area. The
Mathematics I progress page is the reference for this navigation philosophy: the user can understand where they are,
see the parent hierarchy, and move backward without losing context.
The implementation should therefore treat breadcrumb hierarchy as part of the application's information architecture, not
as decorative text.
6. Acceptance Criteria
 Reports landing page provides a clear Calendar → Reports breadcrumb path.
 The Calendar breadcrumb is interactive and returns the user to the Calendar.
 Report detail pages preserve the Calendar → Reports parent hierarchy where applicable.
 The Reports breadcrumb visually matches the established Progress breadcrumb style.
 The existing Progress breadcrumb/navigation behavior remains unchanged and functional.
 Browser back/forward behavior and direct report routes continue to work.
 No duplicate or competing breadcrumb systems are introduced.
7. Implementation Boundary
This is a focused navigation/UI change. Do not modify progress calculations, report data models, storage, planning
logic, or generated plan data to solve it. The implementation should inspect the existing router/app breadcrumb
construction first and make the smallest change that establishes the correct hierarchy across Reports.
8. Reference Screenshots
Figure 5 — Progress section: breadcrumb hierarchy includes Calendar → Progress.
Figure 6 — Reports section: current breadcrumb/header lacks a Calendar return path.
Figure 7 — Mathematics I progress detail: desired hierarchy/back-navigation pattern.
Figure 8 — Overall progress report: reports hierarchy example.
9. Change Log Entry
CHANGE-002 — Correct the Reports breadcrumb/navigation hierarchy so it includes a clickable Calendar parent,
matching the working Progress navigation pattern. Preserve the existing Progress behavior and maintain the full
hierarchy on deeper report pages.
Study Planner — Change & Enhancement
Specification
CHANGE-003  Reports Section — Four Subsections
Change ID
CHANGE-003
Category
Reports UI  Tables  Timetable  Navigation  Data hierarchy
Scope
Reports → Overall Progress → Weekly Timetable Chart → Weekly Report → Daily Report
Priority
High
Implementation order
Strictly follow Section 1 → Section 2 → Section 3 → Section 4
1. Core Objective
Correct the Reports section without disturbing functionality that is already working. The work must be executed
hierarchically: first fix Overall Progress, then Weekly Timetable Chart, then Weekly Report, and finally the small Daily
Report spacing issue. Each subsection should be verified before moving to the next.
Important: this change is primarily about presentation, hierarchy, navigation and accurate use of the existing
study-week/date data. Do not rewrite working progress calculations, task completion logic, or file-export logic merely to
solve these UI issues.
2. Section 1 — Overall Progress
Problem A — Table column/row alignment
The tables shown inside Overall Progress are visually misaligned. Header cells and their corresponding data cells do
not remain in one consistent vertical column/row structure. Content from one row visually drifts toward the next row,
making the table difficult to scan.
Required result: every header must define one stable column, and every row's value must remain directly under the
correct header and aligned with the same column across all rows. Apply this consistently to the affected tables in the
Overall Progress section.
Problem B — Preserve HTML export
The Export HTML functionality is already working correctly. It must remain fully functional and must not be broken or
redesigned as part of this change.
Negative requirement: do not change the Export HTML action, export generation flow, or its working behavior. Only
correct the on-screen presentation/alignment of the report tables.
3. Section 2 — Weekly Timetable → rename to “Weekly Timetable
Chart”
3.1 Rename
Change the report-card/section name from Weekly timetable to Weekly Timetable Chart. Use this terminology
consistently wherever this report is presented.
3.2 Show all four weeks before opening a chart
Clicking Weekly Timetable Chart should not immediately drop the user into Week 1 only. First show a Week-selection
view containing all four study weeks: Week 1, Week 2, Week 3 and Week 4. The user then clicks a week to open that
week's actual timetable chart.
This selection view should establish that all four weeks exist and are accessible. It does not need to show progress
percentages if the existing design does not require them; its primary purpose is week selection and discoverability.
3.3 Use stored study-week date ranges
The timetable chart must use the canonical study-week data rather than independently inventing or shifting dates. For
the current cycle, Week 1 is 2026-10-02 → 2026-10-08. Therefore the chart's first study day must be Friday, October 2,
not October 1.
The same principle applies to Weeks 2–4: their displayed dates must come from the same stored study-week/date
mapping used by the Calendar and Reports data.
3.4 Correct time-axis formatting
The current chart displays times in a 24-hour-like sequence such as 12:00 followed by 13:00. Replace this with a
human-readable 12-hour clock: after 12:00 comes 1:00 PM, then 2:00 PM, etc.
AM and PM should be visually distinguishable using the intended design treatment (for example, different text colors),
matching the supplied desirable reference rather than showing a raw 13:00/14:00 sequence.
3.5 Hide non-useful break/gap rows
The timetable currently exposes grey break/gap blocks. These are not useful to the user's primary timetable view and
should not occupy prominent chart space. Remove/hide these break-only visual blocks from the chart presentation so
the study schedule is the focus.
Do not interpret this as deleting the underlying schedule data. This is a presentation requirement: the chart should not
visually emphasize empty/break periods that the user does not need to inspect.
3.6 Remove unnecessary internal scrollbar
The Weekly Timetable Chart currently shows an unnecessary scrollbar on the right side of the chart area even though
there is no meaningful horizontal/vertical content requiring that internal scroll container.
Remove the unnecessary internal scrollbar while preserving normal page scrolling.
Negative requirements: the timetable chart's working file/export/download functionality is already correct. Do not break or
unnecessarily rewrite it. Do not add a scrollbar back unless the chart genuinely requires scrolling after the layout is
corrected.
4. Section 3 — Weekly Report
4.1 Expose all four weeks
The Weekly Report currently opens with Week 1 only, leaving the user without an obvious way to inspect Weeks 2–4.
Provide a four-week selection layer first: Week 1, Week 2, Week 3 and Week 4.
Each week must be selectable. After selection, open that specific week's report/progress data. If a future week has no
completed tasks, show its real zero progress rather than hiding the week.
4.2 Fix Weekly Report table alignment
The Weekly Report's days/progress table has the same structural presentation issue: values visually drift between
rows/columns. Each row must remain a clean row, and each column must stay vertically aligned with its header.
Do not solve this by merely changing text size. The underlying table/grid layout must provide stable column widths, row
boundaries, padding and alignment.
5. Section 4 — Daily Report
5.1 Small spacing issue in the Schedule table
The Daily Report is otherwise functioning correctly. In the Schedule table, one row's content is visually too close
to/drifts toward the following row. Correct only the affected row spacing/padding so the row boundaries read cleanly.
5.2 Tasks table is already correct — DO NOT TOUCH
The Tasks table in Daily Report is considered fixed and should be preserved exactly in behavior and layout. Do not modify
its row structure, spacing, column alignment, styling, or data rendering while fixing the Schedule table.
6. Strict Implementation Hierarchy
 Step 1: Overall Progress — fix table/grid alignment; verify Export HTML remains unchanged and working.
 Step 2: Weekly Timetable Chart — rename section, add four-week selector, correct study-week dates, fix 12-hour
AM/PM time axis, hide break-only visual blocks, remove unnecessary internal scrollbar; verify export/download remains
working.
 Step 3: Weekly Report — add four-week selector and correct table row/column alignment.
 Step 4: Daily Report — fix only the small Schedule-table spacing issue; leave the Tasks table untouched.
 Step 5: Final regression pass — verify Calendar/Progress/Reports navigation, existing breadcrumbs,
exports/downloads, progress calculations and direct routes still work.
7. Global Negative Requirements
 Do not break the already-working Progress section.
 Do not break the existing Reports export/download functionality.
 Do not modify the Daily Report Tasks table.
 Do not invent a second independent study-week date system; use the canonical study-week mapping.
 Do not show Week 1 as the only discoverable week where four weeks exist.
 Do not use 24-hour labels such as 13:00 where the desired UI calls for 1:00 PM.
 Do not preserve unnecessary internal scrollbars merely because the current implementation has one.
 Do not delete underlying break/schedule data solely because break rows are hidden visually.
 Do not make broad styling changes outside the specific problems described here.
8. Acceptance Checklist
Area
Pass condition
Overall Progress
All affected tables have stable header → column → row alignment.
Overall Progress
Export HTML still works exactly as before.
Weekly Timetable Chart
Name updated from Weekly timetable to Weekly Timetable Chart.
Weekly Timetable Chart
Week 1–4 selection is visible before a specific chart is opened.
Weekly Timetable Chart
Week 1 displays Fri Oct 2 through Thu Oct 8.
Weekly Timetable Chart
Time axis uses 12-hour AM/PM formatting.
Weekly Timetable Chart
Break-only grey visual blocks are hidden from the primary chart.
Weekly Timetable Chart
Unnecessary internal scrollbar is removed.
Weekly Report
Week 1–4 are selectable; each week's real progress is shown.
Weekly Report
Days/progress table rows and columns are properly aligned.
Daily Report
Only the affected Schedule-table spacing is corrected.
Daily Report
Tasks table remains unchanged.

10. Change Log Entry
CHANGE-003 — Repair the four Reports subsections in a strict hierarchy: Overall Progress table alignment; Weekly
Timetable Chart naming, four-week discovery, canonical dates, 12-hour AM/PM axis, hidden break-only visuals and
scrollbar removal; Weekly Report four-week discovery and table alignment; and the limited Daily Report Schedule
spacing fix while preserving the Tasks table.
Study Planner — Change & Enhancement
Specification
CHANGE-004  Daily Tracker — Actionable Non-Course Schedule Blocks
Change ID
CHANGE-004
Category
Daily Tracker UI  Task interaction  Completion persistence
Scope
Calendar → double-click date → Daily Tracker
Priority
Medium / UX improvement
Affected blocks
Math + Statistics Revision; Daily Review
1. Problem
When a date is opened from the Calendar into the Daily Tracker, the tracker correctly provides interactive checkboxes
for course-related study items. However, two end-of-day schedule blocks — Math + Statistics Revision and Daily
Review — are actionable study/productivity activities but currently appear only as informational schedule cards without
a completion checkbox.
This creates an inconsistent interaction model: the user can mark completion for the course/task blocks above, but
cannot mark completion for these two useful activities even though completing them is part of the daily routine and
provides the same motivational value as checking off other work.
2. Required Change
Make Math + Statistics Revision and Daily Review actionable in the Daily Tracker by adding the same
completion/check-off interaction pattern already used by the existing task cards.
Each of these blocks should contain a visible checkbox (or the same established completion control used elsewhere in
the tracker). The user must be able to click it to mark the activity complete and click again if the existing interaction
model supports unchecking.
The visual and behavioral pattern should feel native to the existing Daily Tracker rather than introducing a new type of
control.
3. Exact Blocks to Make Actionable
A. Math + Statistics Revision
Current role: a scheduled revision activity for weak topics, recall and the error log. Required behavior: add a
completion checkbox using the same interaction pattern as the course/task cards.
B. Daily Review
Current role: an end-of-day review covering completed work, pending items and the next day's plan. Required
behavior: add a completion checkbox using the same interaction pattern as the course/task cards.
4. Completion / Persistence Requirement
These controls must represent real completion state, not merely a visual toggle. The checked state should integrate
with the Daily Tracker's existing persisted-completion behavior so that marking the activity complete remains
consistent with the application's principle that progress is derived from actual completion.
Do not create a separate temporary UI-only checkbox system. Reuse the existing task/completion mechanism where
technically appropriate.
5. Negative Requirements — Do Not Change These
Lunch / Rest, Refresh, Free / Refresh, and other break-only blocks are already correct. They do not need completion
checkboxes and their current presentation should remain unchanged.
Do not turn ordinary breaks/rest periods into tasks merely to make the UI visually consistent. Only the two explicitly
identified actionable activities — Math + Statistics Revision and Daily Review — should gain completion controls.
Do not redesign the Daily Tracker layout, change course-task behavior, or alter existing checkbox styling unnecessarily.
The goal is a targeted interaction enhancement.
6. Implementation Hierarchy
 Locate the Daily Tracker's existing reusable completion/checkbox component or mechanism.
 Apply that same mechanism to Math + Statistics Revision.
 Apply the same mechanism to Daily Review.
 Ensure their completion state persists using the existing completion-storage flow.
 Verify that existing course tasks still behave exactly as before.
 Verify that Lunch / Rest and other break blocks remain non-actionable and unchanged.
7. Acceptance Checklist
Requirement
Pass condition
Math + Statistics Revision
Visible completion checkbox/control is present and usable.
Daily Review
Visible completion checkbox/control is present and usable.
Interaction
Controls use the same established task-completion behavior/style.
Persistence
Completion state is retained through the existing Daily Tracker persistence flow.
Course tasks
Existing course-task checkboxes continue to work unchanged.
Break blocks
Lunch / Rest, Refresh and other break-only blocks remain unchanged and non-actionable.
Scope
No unnecessary Daily Tracker redesign is introduced.
8. Reference Screenshots
Figure 1 — Daily Tracker: lower schedule area showing Refresh, Math + Statistics Revision, and Daily Review.
Figure 2 — Daily Tracker: English study block with interactive task checkboxes.
Figure 3 — Daily Tracker reference showing the existing checkbox/task interaction pattern.
9. Change Log Entry
CHANGE-004 — Extend the Daily Tracker's completion interaction to the actionable Math + Statistics Revision and
Daily Review blocks. Preserve all break-only blocks such as Lunch / Rest and Refresh exactly as they are.
Study Planner — Change & Enhancement
Specification
CHANGE-005  Header Branding Icon Replacement
Change ID
CHANGE-005
Category
Global Header UI  Branding / iconography
Scope
Study Planner header — current SP square logo
Requested result
Replace SP logo with uploaded Task Square SVG in white
Asset
task-square-svgrepo-com.svg (uploaded in this change request)
1. Required UI Change
In the Study Planner's main header, remove the existing purple “SP” logo/monogram and replace it with the uploaded
Task Square SVG icon.
The uploaded SVG should be rendered in white so it fits the existing dark header and visually matches the requested
branding direction.
The replacement should occupy the same general logo position and remain visually balanced with the existing
“Study-Planner” title and subtitle. Do not change the title/subtitle or unrelated header controls.
2. Asset Handling
Use the uploaded SVG file directly as the source asset rather than recreating the icon manually. The asset is already
attached to this request, so no additional file upload is required for this change.
Uploaded asset: task-square-svgrepo-com.svg  viewBox 0 0 24 24  current stroke color #292D32  stroke width 1.5.
Because the uploaded SVG currently uses a dark stroke, apply the required white presentation through the
implementation (for example, an SVG-compatible color/stroke override or an equivalent safe treatment) without
changing the icon's geometry.
3. Visual Requirements
 Replace only the existing SP icon; do not remove the header brand area itself.
